licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported
licenses.note: The reference is Build Guide 0.4.9 at tag v0.4.9. Its repository, settings.gradle, mods.toml and fabric.mod.json all name CC BY-NC 3.0, and its top-level LICENSE is the only licence statement, so its icon and language files are covered by it too.

deviations.what: The fifteen shape generators and their properties are ported and tested as pure logic; nothing is drawn yet, and the library sits in tests/shapes-Test.grug because a grug local function is visible only inside its own file, so code/ could not reach a test.
deviations.why: Stage 1 lands the shapes with the host functions they need, so the rendering API can be designed against a real mod in stage 3, which moves the library into the overlay.

deviations.what: The per-world state and the config are a library in tests/state-Test.grug with no runtime caller yet: nothing loads a state on first access or saves it when a screen closes until the overlay exists.
deviations.why: A grug local function is visible only inside its own file and the host cannot call it, so stage 2 proves both files byte for byte as tests, and stage 3 moves the library into the overlay that reads and writes them.

deviations.what: The state and config files live under the root File.open(r"files") answers, at buildguide/<world>@<dimension>.dat and config/buildguide.cfg, where the reference writes <gameDir>/buildguide/<world>@<dimension>.dat and <gameDir>/config/buildguide.cfg. The host also refuses a name that differs only in case from an entry that is already there, so two worlds whose names differ only in case share one guide here, where the reference on a case-sensitive filesystem kept two.
deviations.why: A mod may write only inside the directory #1757 gives it, so a guide the reference already saved at the game directory's path is not imported and a guide this port saves is not read by the reference. The file formats themselves are the reference's, byte for byte.

deviations.what: A state file whose number does not parse stops the load where it is and keeps what it already applied, where the reference lets the NumberFormatException escape getState() and the client fails the tick. Nothing clamps after a stopped load, so a truncated file can hold an iShapeSet past its shape sets.
deviations.why: grug has no exception to raise, and turning a stopped load into a fresh state belongs to the overlay stage 3 adds. The partial load is exactly what the reference applies before it throws, pinned by _assert_bad_number in tests/state-Test.grug.

deviations.what: The three config comments are the en_us sentences as fixed text, where the reference writes the client's language through Translatable, so a non-English client's rewritten config is not the reference's bytes.
deviations.why: mod_api.json has no entry for a translated string, so a translated comment needs a general host function that a port of any translated mod would use.

deviations.what: The five screens, their widgets and the four key binds are not implemented.
deviations.why: A mod cannot open a screen or draw a filled rectangle yet, and designing that API against more than this port is stage 3 of #1752.

deviations.what: A catenary whose Newton solve does not converge draws no cells: the reference either reports an invalid value or never leaves its loop, and the port answers no cells at once in both cases.
deviations.why: grug cannot raise an error to the player yet. A solve whose values leave the finite range makes the reference throw, and a solve whose Newton step changes nothing (dx 1419, dz 0, an added length of 1) repeats that step until the shape is cancelled. The port ends the solve when a step is non-finite or changes nothing, which bounds both arms, and its cell loops keep the reference's own bounds rather than a cap of this port's own.
